config.title: Berlin Heating Season - FAQ
config.subtitle: When the Berlin heating period starts, the temperatures a landlord owes at each hour, how to measure so the reading counts, and the order of the steps before any rent reduction.

items.q: When does the heating season start in Berlin?
items.a: **1 October, and it runs to 30 April.** That range is a convention drawn from tenancy agreements and court decisions rather than a statute. There is also an earlier trigger: outside the heating period a landlord has to heat when the outside temperature stays **below 12 °C at 21:00 for three days running**. Measured on the hourly ERA5 archive for Berlin Mitte, that happened in September in four of the last eleven years, on 25 September 2018, 19 September 2019, 19 September 2022 and 30 September 2024. The latest it happened was 16 October 2023. Checked on 9 September 2026, this year's forecast keeps Berlin evenings above 15 °C into the third week of September, so 1 October is the date that matters in 2026.

items.q: How warm does my Berlin flat legally have to be?
items.a: Where the tenancy agreement says nothing, Berlin tenant advice treats **20 to 22 °C in living rooms and kitchens and 23 °C in bathrooms** as sufficient during the heating period, between **06:00 and 24:00**. At night the floor is lower and it is the contested figure: Berlin tenant advice accepts that a reduction to **16 °C** can still be lawful, while other guidance puts the night floor at 18 °C. A clause in your contract setting lower temperatures than the daytime figures is generally treated as invalid, because it puts the tenant at an unreasonable disadvantage.

items.q: How do I measure the temperature so it counts as evidence?
items.a: **In the middle of the room, about one metre above the floor.** Not on the windowsill, not beside the radiator, not in the draught by the door. Because **the tenant carries the burden of proof**, one reading on one evening is an anecdote. Berlin tenant advice describes a daily record with readings at several different times of day, kept in a table, covering every room including the ones that are fine. Write down the date and the hour as well as the temperature, because the hour decides which floor applies.

items.q: Can I reduce my rent if the heating does not work?
items.a: Possibly, but **not as the first step**. The order is: log the readings, then report the defect in writing with the rooms, temperatures and hours and a short deadline for repair, three days being the deadline Berlin tenant advice suggests for heating. State that further rent is paid under reserve. Only then look at a reduction, and take advice before you set a figure. Reported rulings run from a few per cent for a flat that reaches only 18 °C to seventy per cent or more when the heating fails outright in the season, and the Landgericht Berlin has granted both ends. A reduction taken at the wrong percentage turns into a rent arrears problem.

Gas and district heating, and very little else. In the 2022 census, with a reference date of 15 May 2022, Berlin had **921,188 dwellings heated by gas and 869,472 by district heating**, together about 89 per cent of the city's flats. Heat pumps, solar and geothermal covered 13,892 dwellings, under one per cent. The distinction matters when something fails: with district heating the heat arrives from outside the building and there is no boiler in your flat to blame, while a Gasetagenheizung sits inside your flat and often carries a gas contract in your name. Paying that gas bill does not move the repair duty from the landlord to you.

items.q: What is the 3 per cent heating cost deduction?
items.a: Since **1 January 2022**, if your building has remotely readable heat meters, the landlord has to send you consumption information **every month**, by app, portal, email or post. Where that information is not provided as required, the Heizkostenverordnung lets you **cut your share of the heating costs by 3 per cent**. It is worth checking how many of those monthly updates you have actually received this year. Separately, meters that cannot be read remotely have to be retrofitted or replaced by **31 December 2026**, so a technician appointment about your radiators this autumn may well be that and not a repair.

items.q: Where can I get free tenant advice in Berlin?
items.a: **All twelve Berlin districts run a free tenant advice service**, funded by the Senate and open to any tenant living in that district. They will look at a temperature log and tell you whether you have a case; representation in court is excluded. The directory of district offices is published on the Senate's own site. Take the printed log with you, because an advisor who can see three days of readings at three times a day gets to an answer far faster than one hearing that the flat feels cold.
